title: zazz SDK source component diagram
description: The modules of the zazz SDK and how a call flows through them. A script registers Handlers and calls zazz::serve, which picks a backend by target: on Unix the native backend reads length-prefixed JSON frames from the control socket on fd 3 with the caller's stdio passed as descriptors; on WASM the backend takes its one call message through the zazz_host imports. Either builds a Call (the per-call context with filesystem, network, clock and environment behind traits) and has Handlers dispatch the message, then answers with a result frame. The zazz::test library in test/ drives the same Handlers over fakes. Everything compiles into the one library; native.rs and fdpass.rs only on Unix, wasm.rs only on WASM.

components.name: zazz SDK source
components.responsibility: The zazz library's modules; lib.rs declares them, re-exports Call, Mode, Error, Result, Handlers, Request, Response and Json, and defines VERSION and serve.

components.name: Entry point (lib.rs serve)
components.responsibility: zazz::serve(handlers): runs the WASM backend on WASM targets and the native backend on Unix.

components.name: Handlers (handlers.rs)
components.responsibility: The script's json-command handler, optional OpenAPI document and service-call operations by operationId; lists the messages they answer and dispatches json-command, openapi and service-call messages, reading the call's mode (agent or human).

components.name: Call context (call.rs)
components.responsibility: Everything a handler can touch during one call: id, mode, exit status, stdio, the Fs, Http, Clock and Env edges with their real implementations (StdFs rooted at the caller's directory, NoHttp, SystemClock, StdEnv), progress notes and the cancellation probe.

components.name: Launcher protocol (proto.rs)
components.responsibility: Frames of a u32 little-endian length and compact JSON, at most 16 MiB, and the hello, ready, result and progress messages; protocol version 1.

components.name: Native backend (native.rs)
components.responsibility: Serves frames on the control socket, fd 3, until shutdown or end of stream: answers hello with ready, runs each call with the three descriptors received with it as stdio, ignores cancel frames (a waiting frame is what the cancellation probe sees), turns a handler panic into a failed result and stops, and exits 70 when the channel fails.

components.name: Descriptor passing (fdpass.rs)
components.responsibility: sendmsg and recvmsg with SCM_RIGHTS through hand-declared C structs for Linux and macOS (no libc crate), at most 8 descriptors per message, and a non-blocking peek for waiting bytes.

components.name: WASM backend (wasm.rs)
components.responsibility: Serves the single call an instance is created for through the zazz_host imports request_len, take, send, http and cancelled; stdio are the caller's, wired by the host; network requests go through zazz_host.http, where the host applies the allowlist.

components.name: HTTP (http.rs)
components.responsibility: Request and Response, their framed wire layout for the zazz_host ABI, https-only URL parsing (no credentials or IP literals), host patterns and the NetPolicy check shared by the WASM host and the fakes.

components.name: JSON and errors (json.rs, error.rs)
components.responsibility: The Json value with insertion-ordered objects, a strict parser limited to 128 levels of nesting, compact and pretty printers and the json! macro; Error, a stable code and a message, with constructors for the codes the launcher understands.

components.name: Human command line (cliargs.rs, render.rs)
components.responsibility: Turns argv into a script's JSON input from the manifest's cli spec (flags, positionals, types, defaults, help) and renders a returned output for a person: strings as they are, lists of flat objects as a table, anything else as pretty JSON.

components.name: zazz::test
components.responsibility: The test library scripts use: a harness that runs the handlers the way the launcher does over a fake filesystem, network, stdio, clock and environment, with JSON, snapshot and schema assertions.
